posts.text: Core CPI in June came in far below expectations, including a sharp slowing in non-housing core services. Put together with PPI, core PCE rose 0.13% in June (1.6% annualized) --*below* a target-consistent pace.

posts.text:
Does the July CPI need to be as soft as the June CPI? No, but it needs to fit the bill of a good CPI. The consensus for core CPI of 0.2% would probably count, though lower is better.

Then the PPI needs to behave too. It's PCE that needs to show disinflation, or a hike is likely.
